notes.headline: Investors looked beyond tech to health care, led by big drugmakers
notes.why: On Tuesday, health care led gains among market sectors and the sector fund reached a record high. Eli Lilly did the most lifting, with UnitedHealth, Merck and others helping. A strategist quoted by Reuters said investors were wary of the AI trade and looking beyond tech, and health care benefited.
notes.name: Health care (Health Care Select Sector SPDR)

notes.headline: Money rotated out of technology into steadier, defensive sectors like real estate
notes.why: On Tuesday, investors stepped back from technology amid doubts that big AI spending will pay off. Reuters said money went into defensive areas, and real estate and utilities were among the winners. The link to this fund is a reading of that rotation.
notes.name: Real estate and towers (Real Estate Select Sector SPDR)

notes.headline: buyers returned to chip makers after an AI-cost scare, ahead of tech results
notes.why: Chip makers bounced back on Monday after a long losing run. Outlets tied the earlier slide to worry over paying for the AI buildout and higher interest rates. They read Monday as buyers returning ahead of company results.
notes.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF

notes.headline: fears that debt-heavy AI builders can't repay loans, and that rates may rise
notes.why: Chip makers were pulled down on Friday in a wider tech slump. Outlets tied it to worry that AI cloud firms such as CoreWeave carry too much debt, and to hotter inflation data that raised fears of higher interest rates. Chip makers had been under pressure all week.
notes.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF

notes.headline: oil climbed to its highest in months as Middle East supply fears grew
notes.why: Oil rose sharply on Friday, to its highest level in months, as worries grew about attacks on shipping and wider fighting in the Middle East. A Russian refinery also paused some work after an attack. The fund holds oil and gas companies, which tend to follow crude.
notes.name: Energy companies as a group (XLE proxy)

notes.headline: worries about the heavy borrowing and spending behind the AI buildout hit big tech
notes.why: Outlets tied the fall in big tech and chip companies on Friday to worries about the AI data center buildout. CBS News pointed to the heavy borrowing behind it, and the AP to doubts about how long the spending will last. CBS also cited rising inflation and rate worries.
notes.name: Nasdaq-100 (QQQ proxy)
